steps.body: A flat shape has **sides** (the straight lines) and **corners** (where two sides meet). A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners. Count the sides, then count the corners — for these shapes they always match.

predict.prompt: You will touch each side of the triangle once. How many touches will that take?
predict.reveal: A triangle has three straight sides. Touch each one and count as you go — that is what “how many sides” means. If you got 2 you skipped a side, and if you got 4 you touched one side twice — go round in order so every side gets exactly one touch.

widget.prompt: Touch each side of the triangle to count it.
widget.successFeedback: 3 sides! You touched every side once. That is what makes it a triangle — “tri” means three.
widget.missedFeedback: There is still a side you have not touched. Go round the shape and get them all.
widget.doubleCountFeedback: You touched one side twice. Tap it again to let it go, then go round in order.

explanationVariants: A square has 4 corners, one at each side-meeting point.
Every side end is a corner: a square has 4 sides, so 4 corners.

widget.prompt: How many corners does a square have?

commonErrors.feedback: A square has one more corner than a triangle: 4 corners.
A square has 4 sides, so 4 corners — not 5.

steps.body: Bigger shapes have more sides. A pentagon has 5 sides and 5 corners; a hexagon has 6 sides and 6 corners. The name tells you the count — "hex" means six.

widget.prompt: Touch each side of the hexagon to count it.
widget.successFeedback: 6 sides! A hexagon has six. Going round in order helps you not lose your place.
widget.missedFeedback: Some sides are still waiting. Keep going round the shape.
widget.doubleCountFeedback: That side is already counted. Tap it again to let it go.

steps.body: A circle is different — it's flat, but it has no straight sides and no corners at all. It's one smooth curve all the way around.

widget.prompt: Touch each corner of the pentagon to count it.
widget.successFeedback: 5 corners! A pentagon has five corners and five sides — they always match.
widget.missedFeedback: There is still a corner left. Look where two sides meet.
widget.doubleCountFeedback: That corner is already counted. Tap it again to let it go.

explanationVariants: Like a square, a rectangle has 4 sides — just not all equal.

widget.prompt: How many sides does a rectangle have?

commonErrors.feedback: That's a triangle's count. A rectangle has 4 sides.
A rectangle needs 4 sides to close up its shape.

explanationVariants: 3 sides and 3 corners is a triangle.
The shape with exactly 3 of each is the triangle.

widget.prompt: Which shape has 3 sides and 3 corners?

options.label: triangle
options.feedback: Yes — a triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.

options.label: square
options.feedback: A square has 4 sides and 4 corners, not 3.

options.label: pentagon
options.feedback: A pentagon has 5 sides and 5 corners, not 3.

steps.body: Use the match, even for a shape you have not named.
explanationVariants: Sides and corners always match — 7 sides means 7 corners, even for a shape you have not named yet.
You do not need the shape's name to answer: sides = corners, always, for every one of these shapes.

widget.prompt: A shape has 7 sides. How many corners does it have?

commonErrors.feedback: Close, but count again — sides and corners always match exactly: 7 sides means 7 corners, not 6.
Sides and corners always match exactly — 7 sides means 7 corners, not one more.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Sides and corners always match: 7 sides means 7 corners.

hints: Sides and corners always go together for these shapes.
You already know 3, 4, 5, and 6 — this one keeps going the same way.

steps.body: Sides and corners always match for these shapes — count one to know the other.
takeaways: A shape's sides and corners are the same number.
A circle has no straight sides and no corners.
steps.teaser: next: telling flat shapes and solid shapes apart.

concept.body: Count a shape's sides (straight lines) and its corners (where sides meet) — they always match. A triangle has 3 of each; a square has 4 of each.

widget.prompt: How many sides does a triangle have?

commonErrors.feedback: That's a square's count; a triangle has 3.
A closed shape needs at least 3 sides.
